title: Flavourings
lead: Real food tastes like itself. When a label lists flavourings, something was added to build the taste. BOTIA shows you what.
tap_hint: Tap an ingredient to see what it is
disclaimer: BOTIA reads what the label declares. Always check important information yourself.
robot_questions: What exactly can the generic word "flavour" or "flavouring" conceal in an ingredients list?
Can "flavouring" include substances consumers expect to see named separately?
robot_answers: "Flavour" or "flavouring" can represent one or many flavouring substances without naming each one. It can also include carriers or solvents that help carry the flavouring and do not always appear separately on the label.

Yes. A generic flavouring declaration can include auxiliary substances or carriers, such as ethanol or propylene glycol, without each appearing separately. That is why the word "flavouring" does not reveal its full composition.
